Find the total area $A$ of the region between the curve $y={x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}$ and the $x$-axis from $x=-1$ to $x=2,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, we find the intersections of the curve with the $x$-axis:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-2{x}^{3} & =0 \\ {x}^{3}(x-2) & =0 \\ x & =0,\,2\end{aligned}
$$

Since $0\in [-1,2],$ we have two regions: 

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=-1$ to $x=0.$

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=2.$

Notice that the region for $x\in [0,2]$ lies completely below the $x$-axis. Hence, the value of

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{4}-2{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x
$$

will be negative. Therefore, the area that we want is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}({x}^{4}-2{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x-2{\int }_{-1}^{0}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}\,{|}_{-1}^{0}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}\,{|}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[{0}^{5}-(-1)^{5}]-\frac{1}{2}[{0}^{4}-(-1)^{4}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[0-(-1)]-\frac{1}{2}[0-1] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x\in [0,2],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =-{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{4}-2{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x+2{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}\,{|}_{0}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}\,{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}[{2}^{5}-{0}^{5}]+\frac{1}{2}[{2}^{4}-{0}^{4}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}[32]+\frac{1}{2}[16] \\  & =-\frac{32}{5}+8 \\  & =\frac{8}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the total area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{10}+\frac{8}{5} \\  & =\frac{23}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
